programme: RBPJ (the Notch/CSL DNA-binding effector), SMAD2 (the TGF-β/activin effector), and CREBBP (CBP/p300, the coactivator both RBPJ-NICD and SMAD2/3 complexes require to transactivate) together with KLF4 (the factor both pathways converge on to set epithelial-vs-mesenchymal and endothelial barrier-gene identity) form a Notch–TGF-β–CBP transcriptional module that drives epithelial/endothelial-to-mesenchymal-type transitions and junctional/barrier integrity.
role_in_a: In cervical cancer the retrieved record documents SMAD2/TGF-β signalling directly driving EMT and stromal remodeling in HPV-positive tumors, and KLF4 being rewired by HPV/SRPK1-dependent splicing in the epithelial transcriptome; RBPJ/Notch is evidenced only indirectly here (a γδT-cell prognostic signature, a miRNA network), and CREBBP appears as an immunotherapy-outcome/neoantigen biomarker rather than as a demonstrated Notch/SMAD coactivator in this tissue.
role_in_b: In stroke all three of RBPJ, SMAD2 and KLF4 are independently and directly documented as endothelial/vascular regulators of the neurovascular unit: RBPJ loss disrupts vascular remodeling (Apelin/Cdc42) and pericyte-endothelial communication, TGF-β1/SMAD2 signalling drives endothelial transcytosis and blood-brain-barrier leakage, and endothelial KLF4 depletion produces age-related neurovascular dysfunction; CREBBP surfaces as a histone-acetylation biomarker of ischemic injury.
shared_axis: The same Notch(RBPJ)–TGF-β(SMAD2)–CBP(CREBBP) module that epithelium uses for plasticity and invasion is reused by endothelium to gate barrier integrity, with KLF4 acting as the identity gatekeeper in both settings; if HPV-driven cervical tumors stress this module toward invasive EMT while ischemic cerebral vasculature stresses it toward barrier breakdown, the same factor set would recur in both diseases even though no study has looked at them together.
reasoning: The module is real and nameable — three of the four carrying factors (KLF4, SMAD2, RBPJ) have direct, disease-specific evidence on both sides, and CBP/CREBBP's role bridging Notch-RBPJ and SMAD complexes is established biology — so this is not an arbitrary list. But nothing retrieved studies cervical cancer and stroke together through this axis, cervix and cerebral vasculature have no anatomical or clinical relationship that would make the pairing obvious, and RBPJ itself is flagged discordant (direction of effect differs across patient groups), so the cross-disease claim rests on inference about a conserved pathway being reused in two tissues, not on retrieved evidence of the pairing itself.
support: PMID 41484386 — SMAD2/TGF-β driving EMT and stromal remodeling in cervical cancer via METTL3/KRAS; PMID 38180377 — SMAD2-linked EMT in cervical cancer via a lncRNA-IGF2BP1 axis; PMID 42385697 — TGF-β1-SMAD2-induced endothelial transcytosis driving blood-brain-barrier leakage; PMID 42215998 — TGF-β1 signalling engineered/targeted in stroke recovery; PMID 41551143 — KLF4 in HPV-driven cervical cancer transcriptome/splicing rewiring; PMID 42313933 — endothelial KLF4 depletion driving neurovascular dysfunction in cerebrovascular disease; PMID 37051908 — RBPJ deficiency disrupting vascular remodeling via Apelin/Cdc42; PMID 36147294 — RBPJ-linked endothelial-pericyte miscommunication in cerebrovascular pathology; PMID 39206965 and PMID 33548740 — RBPJ appearing in cervical cancer prognostic/miRNA-network studies (not EMT-specific); PMID 42004604 — CREBBP as a histone-acetylation biomarker candidate in ischemic stroke; PMID 42332782 and PMID 40826144 — CREBBP appearing in cervical cancer immunotherapy-outcome and neoantigen studies. No retrieved paper studies both diseases jointly through this module.
how_to_falsify: Run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for CREBBP, RBPJ and SMAD2 in parallel in an HPV+ cervical cancer line and in ischemic cerebral microvascular endothelial cells: the shared-axis account predicts co-occupancy of the three factors at KLF4-bound regulatory elements (e.g., near ENG, SERPINE1, ACTA2) in both cell types. If co-occupancy is absent, or if CREBBP occupancy at RBPJ/SMAD2 sites is not lost upon CBP/p300 inhibition in both systems, the proposed shared module does not hold and the concordance is coincidental.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (stroke) versus cervix (cervical cancer) — anatomically unrelated, so overlap could reflect a peripheral/blood transcriptional signature rather than a tissue-intrinsic mechanism. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 39 patient-group comparisons, so the recurrence counts are largely repeated subgroup splits of the same two cohorts, not 39 independent replications. RBPJ and MBD2 pass the target-overlap threshold but are directionally discordant, meaning they do not act uniformly across groups — consistent with Notch's known context-dependent activating/repressive behaviour, but it weakens their standing as a stable module member. Generic-tissue exclusion removed broad blood/immune regulators (STAT1, SPI1, IRF8, NFATC1, IKZF1, AR, VDR, BCL6, CREB5, HLX) — the signal here is not simply routine blood-cell activity, but that does not by itself prove the vascular/EMT story. Several high-recurrence concordant factors (RERE, ZNF350, LHX3, HIVEP3) have no disease evidence at all in either condition and were deliberately left out of the account, illustrating that recurrence alone does not establish relevance.
